dedupe_keys.name: ogc pipelineml conceptual and encoding model standard 1 0 oil and gas pipeline data exchange

description: PipelineML is an Open Geospatial Consortium implementation standard for the interoperable interchange of data about oil and gas pipeline systems. Version 1.0 (document 18-073r2, edited by John Tisdale, approved 25 June 2019 and published 7 August 2019) defines a conceptual model and GML-compliant XML encoding for individual pipeline components, with lightweight aggregation, and was developed by contributors from ten countries including the US, Canada, Norway, the UK, Brazil and Korea. Coverage: the initial PipelineML Core addresses two industry use cases, new construction surveys and pipeline rehabilitation; its component classes include cap, compressor, elbow, flange, launcher-receiver, line pipe, meter, pump, reducer and tap, with requirement classes for linked open data identifiers and code lists. Right-of-way and land management are left to OGC LandInfra, and cathodic protection, facility and safety are named as future extensions. Format and access: the standard is published free as HTML on docs.ogc.org with conformance tests in an abstract test suite; data instances are GML or XML documents. Licence: OGC copyright with the OGC licence agreement, which grants free rights to implement, use, copy, modify and distribute provided notices are kept. Caveats: this is an exchange format, not a dataset of pipelines; the pages read did not show whether example files or XML schemas are published beside the document, and no version after 1.0 was seen. Simulation uses: a common structure for pipeline asset inventories that feed gas and oil network flow and integrity models. Related records: the OGC WaterML 2 family (data-ogc-waterml-2) is a sister OGC exchange standard for water data.
